items.title: Treylon Burks caught 2-of-3 targets for 30 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals.
items.text: While Burks did little in the box score, he drew a defensive pass interference call in the end zone that set up the team’s only touchdown of the game on a Jacory Croskey-Merritt touchdown run on the following play. his three targets finished tied for fourth on the team behind Antonio Williams’ 12, Stefon Diggs’ six, and Chig Okonkwo’s five, leaving Burks in shaky fantasy territory as the team enters the final two months of play. - Mark Garcia

items.title: Stefon Diggs caught 4-of-6 targets for 45 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals.
items.text: Diggs was shown displaying clear frustration on multiple occasions, the two most glaring of which came on the sideline following a poorly thrown ball from quarterback Jayden Daniels. History would repeat in the second half when Daniels bounced a ball to Diggs in the end zone after escaping to his right, the former of whom had broken free of coverage over the middle of the field. items.title: Chig Okonkwo caught 4-of-5 targets for 66 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals.
items.text: The veteran tight end’s five targets finished third on the team behind the 11 of Antonio Williams and six of veteran Stefon Diggs. Okonkwo remains unlikely to return elite volume in the more conservative Washington offense but can continue to return usable fantasy outings as a viable TE2. He’ll push for TE1 status in a plus matchup against the Cardinals in Week 12. - Mark Garcia

items.title: Antonio Williams caught 9-of-11 targets for 122 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals.
items.text: Williams was the top option for quarterback Jayden Daniels throughout, seeing consistent volume throughout. He staked his mark on the game for good with a 42-yard reception to set up the game-winning field goal as time expired, effectively saving the Commanders’ season in the process. After teasing fantasy upside throughout the first half of his rookie season, Williams finally appears to have earned the top role through the air as he enters the final two months of the regular season as a viable WR3 with WR2 upside in fantasy circles. He gets a tantalizing matchup against the Cardinals in Week

items.title: Austin Ekeler rushed seven times for 41 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals, adding three yards on two receptions.
items.text: The box score does little to jump off the page but it is notable that Ekeler played over Rachaad White as the primary change of pace option behind Jacory Croskey-Merritt. Whether that was due to White’s presence on the injury report throughout the week remains to be seen. Either way, the only fantasy-viable back currently on the roster appears to be Croskey-Merritt, leaving both Ekeler and White of little value moving forward. - Mark Garcia

items.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed 13 times for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals, adding 23 yards on two receptions.
items.text: Croskey-Merritt immediately returned from injured reserve to handily lead the team in snaps and opportunities, despite veteran Austin Ekeler playing the team’s first series. More interesting was the fact that Rachaad White hardly had a role, with Ekeler serving as the primary change of pace option, something that could be due to White’s presence on the injury report throughout the week. Either way, Croskey-Merritt appears to have a stranglehold on lead duties moving forward, a role that keeps him as a viable RB2 in the immediate future. That holds true for a Week 12 meeting with the Cardinals.

items.title: Jayden Daniels completed 23-of-35 passes for 289 yards in the Commanders’ 22-20, Week 11 win over the Bengals, adding 55 yards on six carries.
items.text: Daniels and the Commanders were unable to get anything going offensively while playing through driving rain in the first half, going three-and-out on three of their first four possessions before their lone touchdown drive of the game on their final possessions before the break. Things would change in the second half as Daniels led five consecutive scoring drives, all of which ended in field goals, proving enough to eek out a victory that could have saved the team’s season.
